notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\) and edge set \(E\); every edge has a source and a target (the two ends of an undirected edge are interchangeable)

formulas.name: Complement (Harary 1969)
formulas.latex: V(\overline G)=V,\qquad E(\overline G)=\{uv:\ u\neq v,\ uv\notin E\}
formulas.where: Two distinct nodes are adjacent in \(\overline G\) exactly when they are not adjacent in \(G\). For a digraph the pair is ordered: \((u,v)\in E(\overline G)\) exactly when \((u,v)\notin E\), \(u\neq v\). Defined for simple graphs; edge multiplicity and weights have no complement.

variants.graph_complement: The complement operation as listed by one set of tools; same formula.
variants.op_complement: The complement operation as listed by another set of tools; same formula. The convention for self-loops (excluded above, or included for nodes without a loop) is not fixed by the definition.

edge_cases.definition_gives: The complement of the null graph is the null graph.
The complement of an edgeless graph on \(n\) nodes is the complete graph \(K_n\).
The complement of \(K_n\) is edgeless.
The definition for simple graphs has no loops in either graph; whether a missing loop becomes a loop in \(\overline G\) is not decided by it.
Multiplicities are not defined for the complement: the pair is either adjacent or not.
Applied to ordered pairs for digraphs; \(\overline{\overline G}=G\) holds in both cases.

graph_composition.note: Tools use the word 'compose' for at least two different operations (relational composition of edge sets, and the lexicographic product also called composition); the sources do not say which operation each documented entry performs, and a third reading (union with attribute override) is not defined in the sources checked. The relational form is given without a cited source.

notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\) and edge set \(E\); every edge has a source and a target (the two ends of an undirected edge are interchangeable)

formulas.name: Composition (lexicographic product) G[H] (Harary 1969)
formulas.latex: V(G[H])=V\times V_H,\qquad (u,x)(v,y)\in E\iff uv\in E\ \text{or}\ (u=v\ \text{and}\ xy\in E_H)
formulas.where: Replace every node of \(G\) by a copy of \(H\); all edges between the copies of adjacent nodes of \(G\).

formulas.name: Relational composition of edge sets
formulas.where: Path of length 2 whose first edge is in \(G\) and second in \(H\), on a common node set; the order of the operands matters.

variants.op_compose: Either of the two operations above, depending on the tool; the entries of documented-only tools are not specified further in the sources.

formulas.name: Symmetric difference
formulas.where: Edges in exactly one of the two graphs.

variants.op_difference: Edges of the first graph not in the second; the symmetric difference is the same set operation applied both ways (concept graph_symmetric_difference).

\(G-H\) with \(E=\emptyset\) is edgeless; \(G-H=G\) when \(E_H=\emptyset\).

number of edges of a shortest path; \(\infty\) if none

formulas.name: Graph power (Bondy and Murty 2008)
formulas.where: Nodes within distance \(k\) are joined; \(G^1=G\) (as a simple graph). For a digraph use the directed distance \(d(u,v)\).

variants.cat_power: The \(k\)-th power; the entry is documented only and not run.

edge_cases.definition_gives: Nodes in different components have \(d=\infty\) and are never joined, whatever \(k\).
Pairs not reachable along edge directions have \(d=\infty\) and are not joined.
\(k\ge1\) is needed; \(k=0\) joins nothing (the condition \(1\le d\le 0\) is empty) and large \(k\) gives the complete graph on each component.
\(d(u,u)=0\) is excluded by \(1\le d\), so a power has no loops even when \(G\) has them.

graph_products.note: The sources list one collective entry of documented tools; the four products are defined, but which of them each tool computes is not recorded.

notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\) and edge set \(E\); every edge has a source and a target (the two ends of an undirected edge are interchangeable)
second graph, with the same edge conventions as \(G\)
node of a product, \(u\in V\), \(x\in V_H\)

formulas.name: Cartesian product
formulas.where: One factor moves while the other stays.

formulas.name: Tensor (direct, categorical) product
formulas.where: Both factors move at once.

formulas.name: Strong product
formulas.where: The union of the Cartesian and the tensor product edge sets.

formulas.name: Lexicographic product (composition)
formulas.where: The first factor decides unless it stays; not commutative.

variants.op_graph_product: Collective entry for the graph products of documented tools: Cartesian, tensor, strong and lexicographic products have the formulas above; which products a tool offers is not recorded.

edge_cases.definition_gives: A product with a null graph has no nodes.
The product of an edgeless factor is edgeless for the tensor product, and a union of copies of the other factor for the Cartesian product.

A loop in a factor adds edges between a node's copies and others, by the formulas; loop-free input gives a loop-free product except where the formula places loops (the tensor product of two looped nodes).
For digraphs the pairs are ordered in each coordinate.

notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\) and edge set \(E\); every edge has a source and a target (the two ends of an undirected edge are interchangeable)

formulas.name: Reverse (converse) digraph (Harary, Norman and Cartwright 1965)
formulas.where: Every arc is turned around; the adjacency matrix is transposed, \(A(G^R)=A(G)^{\top}\). For an undirected graph the operation is the identity.

variants.cat_reverse: Arc reversal; documented only and not run.

edge_cases.definition_gives: On an undirected graph the reverse equals the graph; on a digraph out-degree and in-degree swap.
A loop \((u,u)\) is its own reverse.
Weights stay on their arcs.

variants.cat_difference_sym: Edges in exactly one graph; the tool entry is documented only and not run.

formulas.name: Union (Harary 1969)
formulas.latex: V(G\cup H)=V\cup V_H,\qquad E(G\cup H)=E\cup E_H
formulas.where: Nodes and edges present in at least one of the graphs; common nodes are identified.

formulas.name: Disjoint union
formulas.where: The two node sets are taken as disjoint (relabelled if needed), so no node or edge is shared and the number of nodes is \(|V|+|V_H|\).

variants.op_union: Either the union (common nodes identified) or the disjoint union (nodes relabelled apart), and the all-graphs forms that fold several graphs; which of the two a function computes is part of its definition.

edge_cases.definition_gives: The union with the null graph is the other graph.
The union with an edgeless graph adds only nodes.

formulas.name: Inverse line graph (root graph)
formulas.latex: R\ \text{is a root graph of}\ H\iff L(R)\cong H
formulas.where: Given \(H\), find a graph \(R\) whose line graph is isomorphic to \(H\); defined only when \(H\) is a line graph, and then \(R\) is not always unique (\(K_3\) is the line graph of both \(K_3\) and \(K_{1,3}\)). See the concept line_graph for \(L\).

variants.cat_inverse_line: The root graph of a line graph; documented only and not run.

edge_cases.definition_gives: The null graph is the line graph of the null graph or of any edgeless graph, so the root is not unique.
A graph that is not a line graph has no root: the operation is not defined for it.
\(K_n\) is the line graph of the star \(K_{1,n}\) (and \(K_3\) also of \(K_3\)).

notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\) and edge set \(E\); every edge has a source and a target (the two ends of an undirected edge are interchangeable)

formulas.name: Line graph (Harary 1969)
formulas.latex: V(L(G))=E,\qquad ef\in E(L(G))\iff e\neq f\ \text{and}\ e,f\ \text{share an end}
formulas.where: One node per edge of \(G\); two are adjacent when the edges meet at a node. \(|V(L(G))|=m\), and node \(e=uv\) has degree \(d_u+d_v-2\) in a simple graph.

formulas.name: Directed line graph
formulas.where: Arc \(e\) leads to arc \(f\) when the target of \(e\) is the source of \(f\); a walk in \(L(G)\) is a walk of arcs of \(G\).

variants.line_graph: The undirected line graph for undirected input and the directed line graph for directed input; the nodes of the result are the edges of the input.

edge_cases.definition_gives: \(m=0\): the null graph.

mycielskian.note: The construction is given from its standard description without a cited primary source (Mycielski 1955 is not among the checked bibliography); the two documented entries are not specified further in the sources.

notation.meaning: graph with node set \(V\) and edge set \(E\); every edge has a source and a target (the two ends of an undirected edge are interchangeable)
the original node \(v_i\), its copy \(u_i\) and the new apex node \(w\)

formulas.name: Mycielskian \(M(G)\)
formulas.latex: V(M(G))=\{v_i\}\cup\{u_i\}\cup\{w\},\quad E=\{v_iv_j,\ v_iu_j,\ u_iv_j:\ v_iv_j\in E(G)\}\cup\{u_iw\}_{i}
formulas.where: Adds a copy \(u_i\) of each node joined to the neighbours of \(v_i\), and an apex \(w\) joined to all copies: \(2n+1\) nodes and \(3m+n\) edges, triangle-free when \(G\) is, and one more colour needed than for \(G\).

variants.cat_mycielski: Mycielski graph as listed by one documented tool; same construction.
variants.cat_mycielskian: Mycielskian of a graph as listed by another documented tool; same construction, possibly iterated.

edge_cases.definition_gives: The construction gives the single node \(w\) (\(2\cdot0+1\) nodes).
One node gives \(M(K_1)=K_2\).

dichotomize.note: The tool entries are documented only; the default cutoff and comparison of each tool are not recorded.

formulas.name: Dichotomization of a valued relation (Wasserman and Faust 1994)
formulas.where: A valued tie is kept as a 1 when it passes the cutoff and dropped otherwise; the choice of \(c\) and of \(\mathrm{op}\) changes the network and is a modelling decision.

variants.cat_dichotomise: Threshold rule \(b_{uv}=\mathbb 1[x_{uv}\ \mathrm{op}\ c]\) applied entry by entry; the comparison and the cutoff \(c\) are parameters. This is the British spelling of the procedure in a documented tool.
variants.cat_dichotomize: Threshold rule \(b_{uv}=\mathbb 1[x_{uv}\ \mathrm{op}\ c]\) applied entry by entry; the comparison and the cutoff \(c\) are parameters. This is the American spelling of the procedure in a documented tool.

edge_cases.definition_gives: A zero value passes the cutoff only when \(c\) and \(\mathrm{op}\) allow it, such as \(x\ge0\).
Negative values pass \(x\le c\) or \(x<c\) but not \(x>0\); the rule has no special case.
Any real \(c\) is allowed; a \(c\) beyond the range of the data gives an empty or a complete relation.

multiplex_coding.note: The sources name the procedure (multiplex coding of several relations into one matrix) in a documented-only tool and give neither a formula nor a source; the coding scheme is not stated.

normalize_ties.note: Formulas are written from the method names in the documented entry without a cited source; the standard-deviation convention of the z-score (population or sample) and the treatment of a zero normalizer are not stated in the sources. Iterative proportional fitting is on the concept ipf.

notation.meaning: the set of entries normalized together: a row, a column, or the whole matrix
mean and standard deviation of the entries of \(S\)

formulas.name: Sum
formulas.where: Entries of \(S\) sum to 1; not defined when the sum is 0.

formulas.name: Mean
formulas.where: Entries have mean 1; not defined when the mean is 0.

formulas.name: Maximum
formulas.where: The largest entry becomes 1; not defined when the maximum is 0.

formulas.name: Z-score
formulas.where: Mean 0 and standard deviation 1; \(s_S\) uses \(n\) or \(n-1\) in the denominator by convention, and is 0 for a constant set.

formulas.name: Euclidean
formulas.where: Unit Euclidean length of \(S\); not defined for an all-zero \(S\).

variants.normalize_ties: Collective entry: the five scalings above applied by row, by column, or by matrix; iterative proportional fitting is a sixth method (concept ipf).

edge_cases.definition_gives: An all-zero row, column or matrix makes the sum, mean, maximum and Euclidean normalizers 0, so the result is 0/0: not defined.
A single entry has \(s_S=0\) (or \(n-1=0\)): the z-score is not defined.
Negative entries are allowed by the formulas; the sum can then be 0 or negative, and normalization by sum no longer gives proportions.

symmetrize.note: Methods are written from the names in the documented entries without a cited source; which methods each tool offers, and the default, are not recorded.

formulas.name: Maximum (union, 'or')
formulas.where: Keeps a tie if present in either direction.

formulas.name: Minimum (intersection, 'and', strong)
formulas.where: Keeps a tie only if reciprocated.

formulas.name: Sum
formulas.where: Adds the two directions.

formulas.name: Mean
formulas.where: Averages the two directions.

formulas.name: Upper or lower triangle
formulas.where: Copies one triangle onto the other; depends on the node order.

variants.symmetrize_methods: Collective entry for the full method set of a documented tool, with dichotomization by density.
variants.cat_symmetrise: Symmetrization as listed by another documented tool; method not specified in the sources.

edge_cases.definition_gives: The diagonal satisfies \(y_{uu}=x_{uu}\) for max, min and mean, and \(2x_{uu}\) for the sum.

Only asymmetric input is changed; a symmetric matrix is unchanged by max, min and mean.

variants.cat_column_directed_direction_from_imput: Node-level imputation of missing rows from the column or the opposite-direction relation; documented only.

ipf.note: The scaling steps are written in their standard form without a cited source; convergence conditions and stopping rules of the documented entry are not recorded.

formulas.name: Iterative proportional fitting
formulas.where: Alternately rescale rows to the targets \(r\) and columns to \(c\) until both hold; it converges to a matrix with those margins when one exists (equal totals, compatible zero pattern), and is not defined for a zero row with a positive target.

variants.cat_ipf: Alternate row and column rescaling to given margins; documented only.
